items.stem: Under the GDPR, pseudonymised data is:

options.text: Outside the scope of the GDPR
options.rationale: Pseudonymised data can still identify individuals with additional information, so it remains personal data.

options.text: Still personal data subject to the GDPR
options.rationale: Correct: pseudonymised data is personal data because re-identification remains possible.
Anonymised data cannot be re-identified; pseudonymised data can.

items.explanation: Correct: pseudonymised data is personal data because re-identification remains possible.

items.stem: A company must respond to a data-subject access request within what default period?

options.text: One month of receipt, extendable in limited cases
options.rationale: Correct: the GDPR sets a one-month default, extendable by two months for complex requests.
72 hours is the breach-notification deadline, not the DSAR deadline.

items.explanation: Correct: the GDPR sets a one-month default, extendable by two months for complex requests.

items.stem: Select TWO lawful bases for processing personal data under the GDPR.

options.rationale: Correct: consent is one of the six lawful bases.

options.text: The data is stored in the EU
options.rationale: Storage location is not a lawful basis.

options.text: Performance of a contract with the data subject
options.rationale: Correct: contractual necessity is a lawful basis.

options.text: The controller prefers not to ask
options.rationale: Preference is not a lawful basis.
Encryption is a safeguard, not a lawful basis.

items.explanation: Correct: consent is one of the six lawful bases.
